property_summary: For any actor that is owner and any newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) sets owner to exactly newOwner; the bug instead sets owner to msg.sender, violating this for any newOwner != msg.sender.

After a successful transferOwnership(newOwner) call by the current owner, c.owner() must equal newOwner for every fuzzed address; the mutant never updates owner, so it violates this for any newOwner different from the current owner.

For any caller and any new owner, transferOwnership must revert unless the caller is the owner (so owner only changes when the owner calls); the mutant lets any caller set owner, so a non-owner call that succeeds changing owner breaks the rule.

For any caller and any new owner, transferOwnership either reverts (when the caller is not the owner) or, on success, sets owner to exactly the requested new owner; the mutant's broken onlyOwner reverts even for the rightful owner, so it fails to update owner for some fuzzed caller/newOwner pair.

For any fuzzed addresses, whoever is the current owner can hand ownership onward and owner() then equals the requested address; the mutant's broken modifier makes every transferOwnership revert, so owner() can never equal a newly requested owner.
For any caller, a call to owned() must succeed if and only if the caller equals c.owner() (the onlyOwner guard); the mutant removes the guard, so a non-owner caller also succeeds, violating the rule.

For any non-zero caller, once that caller has been made owner via transferOwnership, calling owned() from that caller must succeed (onlyOwner permits the owner); the mutant inverts the check so it reverts for the owner, breaking the rule for the fuzzed actor.

For every caller that is not the current owner, calling owned() must revert; the mutant lets a non-owner steal ownership via transferOwnership (owner is set before the require), after which owned() succeeds for that attacker.

For any admissible caller authorized as owner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must set the contract's owner exactly to newOwner; the mutant always writes address(0), so owner() != newOwner whenever newOwner is nonzero.
For any caller that is not the current owner, transferOwnership must revert (only the owner may transfer ownership); the mutant inverts the guard so every non-owner call succeeds, breaking the rule.

property_summary: For every caller, transferOwnership leaves the owner unchanged unless the caller is the current owner; the buggy modifier lets any non-owner caller change ownership.
For any caller other than the owner, calling owned() must revert (onlyOwner); the mutant removes the check so a non-owner call succeeds, which the test detects via the revert flag.

property_summary: For any fuzzed address a, after ownership is transferred to a (by the initial owner address(0)), a call to owned() by a must succeed without reverting; the mutant's always-failing onlyOwner makes owned() revert for every such owner.

For any actor and any newOwner, transferring ownership to newOwner and then calling transferOwnership again from newOwner must leave owner == newOwner; the mutant instead sets owner to address(this), so the second transfer reverts and owner never equals newOwner.
For any admissible caller, a call to owned() by the current owner completes without reverting; the mutant's inserted revert() breaks this for every owner.
